Showroom

Concept 5 · Direction: Apple-inspired: product tiles

Borrows the principles of Apple’s homepage, not its assets: each tile does one job, centred, with a short headline, one line of copy, two text links and a big product image. The hero states the two specialisms in five words; the next three full-width tiles carry the three things a first-time visitor must get: the M5 GPS DHC (trolleys), free fitting (on black, so it reads as a different kind of thing), and membership (with the £60.90 sum as the headline). A two-column grid of smaller tiles then covers more trolleys, the three club brands and approved used. Copy is the shortest of any concept.

Structural changes from the brief’s section order

Every section becomes a tile, so the brief’s order maps directly: hero, three hero-sized tiles (trolleys, fitting, membership), then a grid for range highlights and clubs. The trust row, pillars and reviews band are reduced to one line of fine print under the grid.

Imagery and photography

Large product cut-outs, centred, on flat light or dark tiles; nothing else in frame. The fitting tile needs one excellent photograph of the bay (placeholder for now). Over time, studio-quality renders of the trolleys would lift this concept more than any other.

Headline copy

H1: “Motocaddy trolleys. Custom‑fitted clubs.”

Sub: “The specialist for both, with free fitting in Ringwood and a members’ club that pays for itself.”

Tiles: “Free custom fitting.” · “£60.90 better off.” · “Steer it from your pocket.”

Motion

Subtle: tiles fade and rise slightly into view; product images scale from 96% to 100% as they enter.

Trade-offs

Does wellInstantly premium and calm; the clearest single message per screen; very fast on mobile (one tile per screen); cheap to maintain because each tile is one product and two links.
Weaker onFew products per scroll, so browsing the range is slow; relies on excellent product imagery; the familiar tile pattern may read as ‘Apple-ish’ to some visitors.
Build effortLow. One tile component in two sizes plus a grid; staff can add or reorder tiles in the theme editor.
Photography neededMedium: one great fitting-bay photo; better trolley renders would help.
Suits bestEveryone, especially mobile visitors arriving from ads or search who need the message in one screen.

EG monogram: ‘EG’ as a small Inter Semibold wordmark in the nav, ink on white (suggestion only; the mark itself isn’t being redesigned here).
